title: La cédula
goal: Sit through the whole bureaucracy for one piece of card
culture: Five weeks, four visits and a shoebox of laminated cards with no order to them. The Spanish that gets you through it is four phrases long and every one of them is a way of saying: I have already done my part.

beats.en: I’ve come for my ID card.
beats.good: Vengo por — I have come for. The single most useful opening sentence in any office in the country.
Ya entregué — I already handed them in. Say it before she asks you to do it again, because she will.

beats.es: ¿Y quién le dijo que viniera hoy?
beats.good: Me dijeron, with no particular they, is both true and unarguable. Naming whoever told you would only get them into trouble.

beats.es: (Pone una caja de cartón llena de cédulas en el mostrador.)
beats.good: A shoebox of laminated cards in no order at all. This is the last sentence of a process that took five weeks and it is worth every one of them.
